value: mating-signal duet maintained across an air gap of up to 6 cm between leaves of separate cuttings; no female response at 7 cm; antennal mechanoreceptors not essential for detection
method: behavioural playback and natural-signal tests, signals recorded with a laser vibrometer
conditions: laboratory-reared virgin adults at least 8 days old, eggs from grapevine canes collected on organic farms in northern Italy; gap between upper and lower leaf surface 0.5 to 7 cm; antennae-ablated test used ten pairs (intact males, females without antennae)

source.authors: Eriksson A, Anfora G, Lucchi A, Virant-Doberlet M, Mazzoni V
source.title: Inter-Plant Vibrational Communication in a Leafhopper Insect

quote: Partners established a vibrational duet up to 6 cm gap width between leaves. Ablation of the antennae showed that antennal mechanoreceptors are not essential in detection of mating signals.
note: Crossref lists CC BY 4.0 (unspecified content-version); the repository PDF prints the Creative Commons Attribution License. Results: 'At 7-cm distance between leaves, none of the females responded to MCS' (male calling signal); seven of ten antennae-ablated females responded at a 5 cm gap. Discussion: it was not possible to determine whether signals were detected as air-borne sound or as substrate vibration induced in the leaf; the authors favour substrate vibration. Dominant frequency range of male calling signals 80-300 Hz. Per-gap proportions are in Fig. 1 only, not read. Name printed as Scaphoideus titanus; GBIF match fetch was denied, so the accepted name is not checked against the authority.
